## 3. The evidence that moved it

**The interception thread took three independent hits in one month, all on the
same assumption.** [41291291](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41291291/) (*Nature*) reports that human
premalignant colorectal lesions are polyclonal in origin;
[41528342](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41528342/) (*Cancer Discov*) reports that colorectal precursor
lesions arise from convergence of distinct mutant clones; and
[41380103](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41380103/) (*JCO*) dissolves genomically smoldering myeloma as a
distinct entity, calling it a mixture of MGUS and myeloma. Interception is built
on the premise that a precursor is a single clone caught early. Three papers in
three journals in one month say the unit of the thing being intercepted is not
what the field has been modelling.

**SERENA-6 is the month's most consequential negative, and it is a
patient-reported outcome.** [41125211](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41125211/) (*Ann Oncol*) reports that
ctDNA-guided early switching produces no patient-perceived quality-of-life gain.
SERENA-6 is the trial that made molecular relapse rather than clinical relapse
the trigger for changing therapy — the flagship of the whole ctDNA-as-guide
thread. A PFS benefit that patients cannot feel is exactly the surrogate/endpoint
gap this corpus tracks, and here it appears inside the thread's own best result.

**The neuro-immune axis produced three supports and no refutations**, all
mechanistic and all in top general journals: serotonin driving chemoresistance
([41629655](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41629655/)), a tumour-brain sensory-sympathetic axis restraining
antitumour immunity ([41639447](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41639447/)), and sensory neurons driving
immune exclusion through dense extracellular matrix
([41650969](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41650969/)). The third is the most useful, because it supplies a
physical mechanism — matrix density — for a thread that has mostly trafficked in
signalling.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41643692](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41643692/) (*Lancet Oncol*): blinatumomab non-response predicts
poor survival after CD19 CAR-T. This refutes the sequential CD19-targeting logic
directly — the assumption that failing one CD19-directed modality leaves the next
one unaffected.

Two cards this month are engineering *around* a failure rather than evidence for
or against a target. [41734999](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41734999/) uses engineered macrophages to
address the haematotoxicity that sank CD47 agents;
[41735000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41735000/) proposes depleting TIGIT-high CD226-negative clonal
Tregs as a safer route to TIGIT targeting. Both are filed as supports on
`next-gen-checkpoints`, but note what they are: the target survives only by
being approached through a different cell or a narrower subset. That is the
same manoeuvre as CD47 reappearing in December 2025 as a CAR-macrophage homing
address rather than a drug.

### (b) Method credibility

[41559218](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41559218/) (*Nat Genet*) is the strongest card of the month:
cell-segmentation error frequently *dominates* differential expression,
neighbourhood and ligand-receptor results in imaging spatial transcriptomics.
Read with January's [41519776](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41519776/), two consecutive months now say the
two most common operations in imaging spatial transcriptomics — deciding where
cells are, and testing which genes differ — are unreliable at the base.

[41601205](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41601205/): reported transcription-factor binding-site accuracy is
an artifact of how the negative set was constructed, not of model capacity.
[41580962](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41580962/): drug-synergy deep models ignore chemical structure
entirely, and one-hot drug identity reproduces their reported performance. These
are the cleanest kind of refutation available — the model is replaced by a
trivial baseline and the number does not move.

[41736096](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41736096/): published cfDNA-methylation cancer classifiers carry
demographic bias that inflates apparent performance.
[41742311](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41742311/): a benchmark of LLM agents on single-cell omics
quantifies where they break down on real workflows — the maturity signal for
`agentic-ai` is the arrival of benchmarks, and it keeps arriving as bad news.
